We took our dog here when we first moved to Lisbon, and I'm so happy we did, as our senior is showing progress since she's in their care. It's a great place with kind staff and very good vets, especially Dr Cheila. The fact that they are a hospital and are open 24 hours is a huge plus. The reception staff is super nice, also.

I would like to thank the doctors and staff at AniCura for the care provided to my cat. From a medical standpoint, I have no reason to question the team's professionalism. I felt that everyone treated Koki with care, respect, and dedication.

However, my experience regarding communication and financial transparency was quite different.

Throughout the treatment, I frequently had to ask for clarification on budgets, invoices, and the treatment plan. Costs were changed without clear explanation, and on several occasions, I had to personally compare the initial budget with the procedures actually performed to understand what had been done and what had not been necessary.

As the guardian of a severely injured animal, I needed to receive clear and upfront information about the treatment plan, hospitalization costs, home care, and the overall estimate of expenses. Instead, the information was conveyed in a fragmented way, which made an already very difficult situation even more distressing.

I continue to believe in the medical competence of the team, but I believe that AniCura has much to improve in its communication with clients and in the transparency of budgets and invoices. Clear and predictable communication makes all the difference when a family faces an emergency situation with their pet.

I was at the clinic yesterday with my dog ​​for a consultation that, in my opinion, was an emergency. However, over the phone and without even seeing the animal, they promptly told me that it wasn't.
The appointment was scheduled for 8:15 pm; we arrived on time, but were only seen about 30 minutes later by Dr. Laura.
My dog ​​had a high fever, hadn't eaten or drunk for a day, and was suffering from vomiting and diarrhea. They did tests that detected severe inflammation through the measured values.
Instead of immediately administering an injection to lower the fever and serum to hydrate and stabilize him; protecting the animal immediately, they simply presented me with a quote of €700.
This quote included ridiculous items, such as a 10 kg bag of dog food for a dog that weighs only 5 kg (when, at home, a 1.5 kg bag lasts three weeks).
All of this was accompanied by a vague speech, in which the doctor told me that they were going to "investigate" the case... As if a dog were going there to be experimented on.
I didn't accept the quote because it was unclear and there was a clear lack of empathy and professional negligence. I asked if it would be possible to write a prescription or give something to lower the fever, something I shouldn't even have had to ask for!
The veterinarian simply wrote down on a piece of notebook paper the dosage of paracetamol syrup I should give (which, in itself, is difficult to administer). She also told me that I didn't need a prescription because, being a pediatric medication, it would be easily sold to me. I accepted out of ignorance. However, upon arriving at the pharmacy, the pharmacist informed me that the veterinarian had a legal obligation to write a prescription. After telling him what had happened, the medication ended up being sold to me.
My dog ​​did not improve and, today, I decided to seek a second opinion elsewhere. Yesterday, at this clinic (AniCura), I paid €137.80 for a consultation, tests, and a small amount of food. Today, at the other establishment, my dog ​​was thoroughly examined:
They did urine tests, an ultrasound, and administered antipyretic, anti-inflammatory, and serum with other medication, all by injection. They asked me for photos of his stool and urine, and tomorrow they will examine him again, at no additional cost.
For now, my only duty is to monitor his fever. And for all this, I only paid €95!
I really liked the new veterinarian, who showed an immediate interest in helping.
I deeply regret that there are professionals who prefer mediocrity to excellence. I will not return and will not recommend this clinic because, effectively, the AniCura group has become a money-making machine. Even the false friendliness is noticeable; all that matters there is the money!

My experience with AniCura Arco do Cego was extremely negative and marked the beginning of one of the most painful periods of my life.

We took our kitten, Dean, to this clinic after abnormalities appeared in his tests. We were told that there were some strange intestinal values, but that there was no cause for great concern and that periodic monitoring every three months was sufficient.

We trusted the medical assessment and followed the recommendations exactly.

When we returned for the follow-up, the reality proved very different. Shortly afterwards, Dean was diagnosed with cancer. Like any pet owner who considers their pet family, the first question that inevitably arises is: could the problem have been identified earlier? Did those signs, which were initially not considered worrying, warrant further investigation?

I will never have answers to those questions. What I do know is that we went from a situation presented as controlled to a devastating oncological diagnosis in a matter of months.

From that moment on, a race against time began, with consultations, exams, treatments, chemotherapy, and surgery. Despite all efforts, we ended up losing Dean.

Naturally, no one can guarantee that an earlier diagnosis would have changed the outcome. But it's impossible not to feel frustration and anger when we remember the calm way we were told there was nothing to worry about.

Dean wasn't just a pet. He was family. He was our best friend, our everyday companion.

Unfortunately, my trust in AniCura Arco do Cego has been deeply shaken. I feel that the initial signs didn't receive the attention they deserved, and that doubt will stay with me forever.

I do not recommend this clinic based on my personal experience.

There is another aspect that causes me enormous discomfort and that I consider deeply inappropriate. I find it very strange to see AniCura Arco do Cego posting videos on social media, supposedly funny or intended for entertainment, while veterinarians perform medical procedures and animals are under anesthesia. In my opinion, these moments should be treated with the utmost respect, professionalism, and dignity. When we entrust our animals to a medical team, we expect the focus to be entirely on their well-being and care, not on creating content for social media. I consider this practice extremely distasteful and a worrying demonstration of a lack of sensitivity towards animals and their owners.

Initially, my experience with this clinic was quite positive. I always felt the care was attentive and professional, and previously, when my dog ​​had pancreatitis, he was well looked after and recovered, which made me very confident in the team.

However, unfortunately, my most recent experience was very different and ended very painfully.

My dog ​​was hospitalized twice between the end of last year and the beginning of this year, initially for kidney problems. During the first hospitalization, everything went well and he was discharged in stable condition. However, shortly afterwards, he started to stop eating again and to vomit. My mother and I had to return to the clinic several times in a short period.

Despite a history of kidney problems, we felt the situation wasn't reassessed with the necessary depth – tests weren't repeated at a critical stage, and we were even told that it wouldn't be necessary to bring him in so often, just to call.

On his last visit, he was given medication that left him extremely weak, to the point that we had to return urgently, and he was hospitalized again. Only then were new tests done, which showed that his kidney levels were again very high.

After a few days, he was discharged. My dog ​​left the clinic crying, unable to stand and in evident distress. When we contacted the clinic, we were advised to wait.

Faced with this, we sought a second opinion at another veterinary hospital, where more complete examinations were performed. We were told that a more careful evaluation should have been done earlier. Only then did they start antibiotic treatment, but unfortunately it was too late.

My dog ​​ended up passing away a few days later.

I write this comment with sadness, but also with a sense of responsibility. I know that it is not always possible to avoid such an outcome, but I am left with the feeling that more could have been done, sooner.

I sincerely hope that this feedback will serve as a food for thought and that other animals may receive more careful attention in similar situations.

The whole team is filled with kind, knowledgeable people who genuinely care for your animal. I had to leave my cat overnight here and it was such a relief to know that she would be in such good care. Truly the best

My experience at this veterinary hospital was extremely frustrating and infuriating.

My dog ​​underwent surgery and was hospitalized. Upon discharge, I was informed that I should return three days later for a follow-up appointment. I asked the doctor directly if this appointment would have a cost, and she assured me it wouldn't. On my way out, I confirmed this again with the receptionist, who reiterated that the first post-surgery consultation was free.

On the scheduled day, I attended the follow-up appointment, and at the end of the consultation, they tried to charge €22. I refused to pay, as I had confirmed twice that there would be no cost. Only after insisting and asking them to call the doctor did they decide not to charge. This was an unnecessary and embarrassing situation that demonstrates a complete lack of consistency in the information given to the client.

That same evening, I realized I didn't have enough antibiotics until the next follow-up appointment, as the doctor had extended the treatment for several more days. I called the hospital and the receptionist, who was very friendly, informed me that I could send the prescription to buy the medication at another clinic or that I could go there to purchase it. I confirmed if they were open 24 hours, as I could only go later, and they said yes.

I went to the hospital after 10 pm and was informed by another employee that, since it was past 9 pm, I could buy the medication, but I would have to pay an additional night fee of €12, because after that time they only attend to emergencies and couldn't "waste time" selling medication.

I explained that I live far away, that my dog ​​had been discharged only three days ago, that he was under observation at that hospital, and that I absolutely needed the antibiotic at 8 am the following morning. Even so, the employee simply repeated that "those were the rules." She even questioned why I hadn't checked the medication earlier, saying that I had gone there at 2 pm and hadn't noticed that I didn't have enough pills.

I explained that the doctor herself also didn't confirm the amount of medication available, nor did she check the report to see if it would be sufficient for the additional days—it was a joint failure. Even so, the receptionist didn't even bother to try to find a solution, speak to a manager, or consider an exception, given that this wasn't a casual client, but a recently operated animal under active care at the hospital.

The lack of sensitivity, empathy, and consistency in the information provided is unacceptable. After everything that has already been paid for the surgery and hospitalization, the least one expects is professionalism, organization, and respect—especially when it concerns the continuity of essential treatment for an animal that has just undergone surgery.

Unfortunately, I felt internal disorganization, constant contradictions, and a total lack of consideration for the client. I do not recommend them.

My Bia has always been well cared for at the Arco do Cego Veterinary Hospital. In recent years, with age, other problems have arisen, including two surgeries and a complicated hospitalization. Dr. Rita oversaw this hospitalization and calmed me down during what is always a very confusing, intense, and potentially reactive time. Thank you! But I must highlight Dr. Laura Pinheiro, who has been caring for Bia since her last surgery until this recovery period from this acute episode. Her enthusiasm, professionalism, care, clarity in her explanations, and above all, her empathy are incredible. One can be an excellent expert in the field, but without beautiful human qualities, that professional becomes incomplete. This is not the case here: Dr. Laura is whole, as Ricardo Reis would say. Many congratulations and thank you for everything!

We are furious and heartbroken. In this hospital people seem nice and they do respect the animals, which unfortunately can't be said of other, equally expensive hospitals. However, all kindness and professionalism is for show and for show only.

We are not professionals and kept our doubts to ourselves when they treated our first cat, who ended up passing away at this hospital - but only after a bill of over 1.400€ was paid accross two weeks of 'treatments'. They kept us waiting for hours when he came to his last visit, already bleeding from the nose and just in a tragic state. Looking back, they surely knew from the start he didn't stand a chance.

Last week we brought our second cat. He was hit in the head with the vaccum cleaner, and being very old, he was deeply traumatized. We rushed in panic to the hospital. They demanded 344€ just to accept him. While in our first cat's visit they suggested I could pay half of the amount the next day, this time 314€ weren't enough - I had to call my mother at 11h30 pm and ask for the remaining 30€ or else.

In the following days a charade unfolded. Our 12 year old cat needed to see a neurologist, needed an ecography, needed so many procedures... I'm a 40 yo Portuguese and seen this often before, standard practice in human private doctors 25 years ago, tons of needless exams that cost fortunes and serve no useful purpose  other than enriching dodgy people. I stated clearly and repeatedly that I just wanted my cat at home, receive the results for all the exams already paid, and take care of my adopted son with a trusted veterinarian.

They insisted, ensured the new exams would not be costly as much of the 344€ had paid for exams not yet made, etc. Professional pose, serious pose, fake kindness, and all the rest of the show. In spite of our repeated calls to take the cat home, he had to stay at the hospital two more days. When we came to get him, surprise surprise, a 400€ bill.

We wrote in the livro de reclamações, and we told these people very clearly exactly what we thought of their practices. And now, two days later, we are still waiting for the results of the last analyses.
Impeccable service. More than approved.
My experience was horrible. We signed the responsibility form and I brought it home today, it's fine. They exploit people's sensitivity just to take money and give sedatives to the animals.

My puppy was in terrible shape; if I hadn't taken him out of there, he would have died. They even did a neurologist consultation, but it was too early, and the visits were too late. The dog wasn't even reacting; they said recovery would take 3 months and they weren't sure he would be okay. I brought him home on a Tuesday, and he started to react; he's already running around the house. He would have died there. It was a very bad experience, and they only tried to rip you off. You pay for something they didn't even do to the animal. I don't recommend them.
They're amazing :) 5 ⭐️

Our dog, Muffin, passed away at the Arco do Cego Veterinary Hospital, and what we experienced was profoundly inhumane. At the moment of loss, the priority was asking if we wanted a joint or individual cremation, with prices presented immediately, without any empathy or support.

We requested a necropsy and are still awaiting the results, without any updates or clear information about the body's fate. We don't know if it was cremated, when, how, or if our request was respected.

The information about the cremation was inconsistent and contradictory: on the day of death they said we could choose; the next day they confirmed it verbally; when we formalized it by email, they called to say that individual cremation was no longer possible. A chaotic management, at a time when the owners are already devastated.

We left this process in shock, not only because of the loss, but because of the way we were treated. A hospital that deals with grieving families cannot operate in this way. We do not recommend them and sincerely hope they review their processes and training.

This is not a hospital, it's a graveyard. I buried two cats with them, and it took me a year to gather the strength to write this review. They will be kind to you, answer your questions, and pretend they care, but the only thing that truly matters to them is profit.

I remember at the end of everything, while I was waiting to collect my cat’s body, the head doctor completely ignored me and kept me waiting for ages just to answer phone calls, clearly prioritizing new clients and more revenue over basic compassion.

We trusted three different doctors to care for my cat, who was always healthy and regularly checked every three months because of his age. When he started losing weight and eating less, I went back multiple times, but they kept insisting he was fine. Eventually, they suggested dental surgery. After sedating him, they found a hole in his throat that would've been easy to see for a doctor, it kept getting worse, something they had completely overlooked before. They apologized again and again, fully aware of their negligence.

The hygiene standards are horrifying. Anyone can enter the surgery room without proper sanitation. Nurses and doctors walk around without gloves or clean uniforms, even the surgeon had shown visible wounds in his mouth without even gloves. The entire place reeks of artificial scents, clearly used to mask the odor of decay and poor hygiene.

Since then, I’ve taken my other cats to a different hospital in Lisbon, where the team actually cares and behaves like real professionals.

Avoid AniCura Arco do Cego at all costs. They don’t care about animals or people, only about financial gain.

I went to get an ultrasound for my dog ​​and came back delighted with the service. From the reception, to the assistant whose name I unfortunately forgot to ask but who was a sweetheart and had the greatest patience with him, the intern, and especially Dr. Filipa.
We need more doctors like her who have love for animals and their profession.
She made a point of evaluating my dog ​​completely, trying to find out where his discomfort was coming from, and not giving up on him even when he was at a high level of stress.
Congratulations to the whole team. I will definitely recommend them and will always come back 🙏🏽🙏🏽

I am writing to file a complaint regarding the behavior of the staff at the veterinary hospital located in the Arco Cego area of ​​Lisbon. I have repeatedly observed that the staff at this clinic, when they go out to walk the dogs they care for, show no concern whatsoever for keeping the public area clean.

The animals relieve themselves in the streets and nearby public spaces, including the Arco Cego garden, and the staff simply continue walking, leaving feces scattered everywhere. This lack of care is unacceptable, especially considering that these are people who work at a veterinary institution, which should set an example in terms of hygiene, civic-mindedness, and respect for public space.

This situation creates a dirty and unpleasant environment for residents and those who frequent the area, in addition to representing a public health problem.

I request that the competent authorities—or the management of the veterinary hospital itself—take urgent measures to correct this situation, ensuring that staff comply with cleaning standards and always collect animal waste during walks. Public space belongs to everyone and should be treated with respect.

Sincerely, Andrey Kolesnikov

The clinic staff doesn't care about your pets. When they're walked in the park across from the clinic, they don't even look after them and never clean up after them. Shameful! Keep your pet away from these pet-hating individuals and the people around you.
